waitpid status=0x8b00 -> WIFEXITED(139) not WIFSIGNALED: the forensics handler ran with SIGSEGV BLOCKED (no SA_NODEFER) so raise() only made it pending and _exit(128+sig) ran -> the probe classifier misreported a FAULTED probe as REFUSED -> parent re-faulted ('post-probe residual' mystery of W14, fully explained)

contract_chain.fix: crash_forensics handler sigprocmask(SIG_UNBLOCK) on the faulting signal before raise -> death is genuinely signal-class; probe verdict honest

contract_chain.evidence: static ELF forensics of the extracted copy: DT_INIT_ARRAYSZ=8 @0x524e0 with init_array[0]=0x0 UNRELOCATED (no R_X86_64_RELATIVE covers the slot) and DT_FINI_ARRAYSZ=16 @0x52420 with fini_array[0]=0xd9b0 (relocated, real dtor) + fini_array[1]=0x0 (unrelocated). The loader calls entry 0 -> rip=0x0. halma's libgdx.so has NO DT_INIT_ARRAY tag at all — the exact structural difference between the family's clean loader (halma) and the faulting one (p9)

contract_chain.fix: native_dep.cpp elide_bionic_skipped_cdtor_entries(): in the runtime-owned extracted copy ONLY, shrink DT_INIT_ARRAYSZ/DT_FINI_ARRAYSZ to drop TRAILING entries whose raw value is 0 or -1 AND carry no relocation. Bionic call_function/call_array skip null/-1 entries (device truth: p9 is a shipped app); glibc calls every entry. Trailing-only shrink never moves entries so existing relocations keep pairing; relocated slots are never dropped; APK bytes untouched. Same surgery class as the CONT-83 bionic versym strip; trace row native.nullcdtor lands honestly

contract_chain.incident: first elision build wrote the new size at the Elf64Dyn d_tag offset (+0) instead of d_val (+8) -> tag became 0=DT_NULL mid-table -> loader's dynamic parse stopped early -> call_init faulted on missing l_info[DT_INIT_ARRAYSZ] (ld-linux +0x5d98 'mov 0x8(%rax),%rdx' with rax=0, fault_addr=0x8) — the FAULT-IP row caught the self-inflicted bug the same day it was introduced; fixed by rewriting the whole Elf64Dyn entry
